note: Memory budgets (issue #13; docs/design/performance.md section 3.1). Checked by scripts/check_memory_budget.py, which runs tests/benchmarks/memory/memory_sizes_probe.cpp and applies the two-sided ratchet in scripts/memory_budget_ratchet.py -- the same policy as tests/golden/perf/preview_budget.json: an entry fails when it is worse than its budget by more than tolerance.worse, AND when it is better by more than tolerance.better (the budget went stale and must be tightened with --update, which refuses to loosen any entry). THE ROWS ARE SPLIT BY REPRODUCIBILITY, NOT BY IMPORTANCE. The `enforce` rows are exact: sizeof of a hot type is fixed by the ABI, and an allocation count comes from a replaced global operator new inside one process, so the probe's two runs must agree byte-for-byte before the gate compares anything. That is why their band is 0%/0% -- it is a real invariant, not noise cover. The `warn` rows are resident memory read from the OS; they move with page granularity, allocator behaviour and machine load, and the two lanes disagree even with identical sizeof(Node): 364 bytes/node on Windows x64 (MSVC) versus 327 on Linux x64 (GCC 13), both Release. A gate that fails at random gets deleted, so those rows report a trend inside a generous band and never block; the bound that does block a leak lives in the CTest tests memory_steady_state and generated_ui_memory, which allow an order of magnitude. The `unmeasured` rows are declared with a reason and NO budget, and the validator rejects a budget on one: Android PSS needs an Android sample this repo does not have (V1 targets Windows and Linux), and the GPU category split needs a Vulkan allocator while every deterministic measurement here uses the null backend, which reports zero allocator bytes by design.

source.probe: tests/benchmarks/memory/memory_sizes_probe.cpp (CMake target memory_sizes_probe); scripts/memory_budget_measure.py runs it and parses its name=value lines
source.ctest: `memory_sizes` runs the probe; `memory_budget` runs scripts/check_memory_budget.py --check --sizes-only in a lane that has a build tree. Not in scripts/gates.py: that aggregator runs in a job with no build directory, so a gate needing a compiled probe cannot live there (the same reason the preview budget runs in pages.yml)
source.argued_by: tests/unit/node_size_tests.cpp already asserts sizeof(Node) <= kNodeSizeBudget at compile time and counts the lazy-allocation costs; tests/golden/memory/*.txt are the CTest leak guards. This file records the same quantities as data so a change shows up as a diff, and it widens the guard to the other hot types
source.conditions: Windows x64, MSVC (vs2026-release preset), 16 logical cores, idle machine; Linux x64, GCC 13.3, Release, 12 cores under WSL2. sizeof rows agree on both lanes except sizeof_computed_style, which is deliberately NOT pinned here because the standard library decides it (std::map handle: 16 bytes on MSVC, 48 on libstdc++); the portable per-node style cost is the recorded computed_style_one_property_bytes, which is 96 on both. MEASURED FROM A RELEASE BUILD ONLY: MSVC Debug measures sizeof_node 320, sizeof_paint_data 536, paint_slot_bytes 624, computed_style_one_property_bytes 208 and plain_node_allocations 2 (a checked-STL proxy allocation), which are different claims about the same code -- measurement.build_config records which one this file pins and the gate refuses a measurement from another configuration instead of reporting it as a regression
source.statistic: sizeof and allocation counts: exact (two runs must agree, else the gate fails). resident bytes: min over rss_runs

measurement.statistic: sizes: exact (every run must agree); rss: min

sizeof_node.measures: sizeof(ui::Node): one plain View node, the number a 10k-node screen multiplies. kNodeSizeBudget is 328, so this row both pins the measured 320 and leaves the 8-byte headroom visible as a diff. Identical on both lanes (320), which is what makes a 0% band honest. Was 312 before the member reorder of security review finding C4 removed 8 bytes of internal padding, then 304; 304 -> 320 is issue #735 slice C, which caches each subtree's paint box in one rhi::Rect. That 16 bytes is a real growth, not reclaimed padding: MSVC's layout dump shows all 304 bytes of the old object occupied, so there was nothing to pack it into. It buys a 4.1x paint-dirty frame (0.375 -> 0.083 ms at 6,001 nodes), which is the trade the budget exists to make visible

sizeof_input_event.measures: sizeof(ui::InputEvent): the element type of the 256-event input queue (about 80 KiB). Deterministic; was 'measured, not yet asserted' in performance.md section 3.1, and this row is the assertion. Identical on both lanes. Was 344 before the member reorder of security review finding C5 removed 24 bytes of internal padding

sizeof_paint_data.measures: sizeof(ui::PaintData): the lazily allocated paint payload a text or image node carries. Identical on both lanes. 536 since issue #617 added the conic shape to the gradient payload (one stop array, the sweep's start angle sharing the union with the linear angle and the radial geometry, plus the shape tag); 528 since issue #731 reordered LinearGradient by alignment, which removed 8 bytes of internal padding. See paint_slot_bytes for what a text node actually allocates

sizeof_pace_decision.measures: sizeof(runtime::PaceDecision): returned by FramePacer::ready() on every tick. Was 24 with `bool, double, bool`, which put 7 bytes of padding after the first bool and 7 more at the tail; issue #731 ordered the members widest-first. Identical on both lanes

sizeof_adaptive_quality_sample.measures: sizeof(runtime::AdaptiveQualitySample): the adaptive-quality observation the frame loop compares each tick. Was 32 with the `double` after two bools (6 bytes of padding before it, 6 at the tail); issue #731 ordered the members widest-first. Identical on both lanes

sizeof_overlay_placement.measures: sizeof(ui::OverlayPlacement): one placed overlay, held per overlay node. Was 48 with the two enums between the anchor and `gap` (6 bytes of padding before the float, 6 at the tail); issue #731 ordered the members widest-first. Identical on both lanes

sizeof_node_id.measures: sizeof(ui::NodeId): the id stored in every side table (paint cache, resolved-style table, dirty list, damage rects). A wider id multiplies every one of them. Identical on both lanes

sizeof_paint_op.measures: sizeof(ui::paint::PaintOp): one recorded sink call in the per-node paint cache. The cache charges ops.capacity() * sizeof(PaintOp) against its 2 MiB budget, so this number decides how many nodes it can hold. Was 2376 while every payload sat inline (GradientDraw 704 + RadialGradientDraw 712 + ConicGradientDraw 712 + BackdropDraw 68); issue #731 made the payload a std::variant and moved the three gradient shapes to PaintRecord::gradients, which is what makes the common op small. Identical on both lanes

sizeof_paint_record.measures: sizeof(ui::paint::PaintRecord): the replayed value of one node, held per cache entry. Grew from 160 when issue #731 added the gradient side-table vector, which is the trade that shrank PaintOp by 2272 bytes. Identical on both lanes

sizeof_background_layer_list.measures: sizeof(ui::style::BackgroundLayerList): the resolved `background-image` value, returned by value from resolve_layers once per painted node. Was 4552 because GradientValue carried all three shapes side by side (24 stops where a gradient can use 8); issue #731 made the three shapes a union, so GradientValue is 200 and the list 1672. Identical on both lanes

computed_style_one_property_bytes.measures: bytes the first property insert into a ComputedStyle allocates (two allocations since the copy-on-write storage of issue #711: the shared block with its control block, digest and vector header, and the vector buffer holding the one pair). A copy of a style allocates nothing, which is what the layout input, the diff baseline and every reader pay now, so the per-node cost that matters fell by about 30x while this one-property floor rose from 64. This is the portable row; sizeof(ComputedStyle) itself is not pinned because it is a std::map handle whose size the standard library decides (16 on MSVC, 48 on libstdc++) and pinning it would record a libstdc++/MSVC difference as a memory budget. 96 on both lanes

plain_node_allocations.measures: global operator new calls made by constructing one plain ui::Node: the node allocates itself and nothing else, so a lazily added default table fails here. Counted, not sampled. 1 on both lanes

aria_table_bytes.measures: bytes the first set_aria allocates; exactly one allocation, so the count is deterministic. 520 on both lanes

inline_style_table_bytes.measures: bytes the first set_inline_style allocates (one allocation). 520 on both lanes

event_binding_table_bytes.measures: bytes the first bind_event allocates (one allocation). 200 on both lanes

paint_slot_bytes.measures: bytes a text node's first set_paint_data allocates (the PaintData copy into the node's optional slot). 536 on both lanes: 536 was the two-shape payload, and issue #617 added the conic shape to the same struct (one stop array, the sweep's start angle sharing the union with the linear angle and the radial geometry) so a node still paints one background image. The 8-byte growth was the start angle plus the shape tag's alignment, not a second stop array; issue #731 then reordered LinearGradient by alignment, which removed those 8 bytes of padding again

cleared_table_reallocations.measures: allocations made by re-setting the aria, inline-style and event-binding tables AFTER clearing them. 0 is the invariant node_size_tests also asserts: clearing keeps the storage, so toggling a value never reallocates

resident_bytes_per_node.measures: resident bytes the process grows per plain node while a 20k-node tree is built (the memory_steady_state quantity). WARN because it is an OS reading of a heap: measured 364 on Windows x64 and 327 on Linux x64 with identical sizeof(Node)=304, and it moves with page granularity and with whatever else the machine is doing. The 300% worse side is a leak detector, not a ratchet on a specific byte count; the 20% better side notices a real win. Enforced as a generous bound inside the CTest test; this row ratchets the trend. sizeof(Node) is 320 since issue #735 slice C, but this row is deliberately NOT re-pinned to match: it is an OS reading with a 300% band, so a 16-byte-per-node change is far inside the noise it already tolerates

node_dirty_scratch_bytes.measures: resident growth across 300 idle dirty-mark/clear cycles after warm-up: the leak guard. Measured 0 on both lanes. WARN, and 0 is allowed for a warn row because 'no growth' is the claim; the allowance is tolerance.worse, so an order-of-magnitude jump warns rather than failing a run

android_pss_bytes.measures: the Android PSS split (Java/Native/Graphics) of a running sample, the number that exposes DPR-squared bitmap scaling and swapchain growth on a phone
android_pss_bytes.reason: NOT MEASURABLE IN THIS REPO'S LANES. Issue #13's motivating number is an Android PSS split (Java/Native/Graphics), and the DPR-squared bitmap scaling it exposes is the point of the mobile row. This worktree has no Android sample and no emulator job, and AGENTS.md makes Android an advisory, post-V1 platform (Windows and Linux are the gating lanes), so there is nothing to run dumpsys meminfo against. No budget is recorded on purpose: a plausible-looking number would read as evidence and would ratchet a figure nobody measured. Declare it until the Android sample and its emulator job exist

gpu_vma_category_bytes.measures: vmaCalculateStatistics bytes by category (swapchain, glyph-atlas pages, images, buffers), the GPU half of the memory story
gpu_vma_category_bytes.reason: NOT MEASURABLE ON THE NULL BACKEND, the backend every deterministic measurement here uses. Issue #13 asks for vmaCalculateStatistics by category. rhi::Device::memory_statistics() reports zero on the null backend by design, and tests/gpu/rhi/rhi_memory_tests.cpp asserts that zero, so a null-backend run cannot produce this row. The Vulkan backend does fill it from vmaCalculateStatistics and rhi_memory already asserts the per-resource costs (a 1024x1024 R8 atlas page is 1 MiB, a 1280x720 RGBA target 3.5 MiB, 17.6 MiB at 4x MSAA), which is the enforcement that exists today. The swapchain category is driver-owned and not counted at all, so there is no number to record for it either
